target_customer: Marketing teams and retailers that run social video ads and pay for automated, templated video creative
problem: Producing and testing many versions of video ads, especially for Facebook and Instagram, is slow and costly for marketing teams.
business_model: B2B SaaS for video ad creative automation

founders.name: Josh Dorward
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CEO on the YC page; became Managing Director of Cloudinary's Video Creative Automation business after the acquisition.

founders.name: Kenji Hashimoto
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automated rendering of templated video from product feeds and ad platform APIs, with optimization analytics, is standard engineering with some media pipeline difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Template driven video generation was copyable by ad tech and creative tools; integrations with ad platforms gave only light switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in sourced material. Cloudinary, a media platform, bought the team and product in January 2022 as its first acquisition, keeping existing integrations including Adobe.

market_need_then: Brands were shifting spend to social video ads in 2017. A TechCrunch Demo Day summary, seen only as a search snippet, said Indivio cut one customer's cost per acquisition by 25 percent.

branding.domain_note: Used the indiv.io domain; it now redirects elsewhere. Exact acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found, and the name is confusable with a Dutch consulting firm and similar names such as Individeo.

pivots.from: Personalized video for business outcomes across the marketing funnel (YC description)
pivots.to: Automated video ad creative for social campaigns (as described at acquisition)
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; the two descriptions differ, so this may be a repositioning rather than a documented pivot.

outcome_analysis: Indivio raised only a small seed after YC, reportedly around 120 thousand dollars, and stayed a small team of about eight. In January 2022 the whole team joined Cloudinary in that company's first acquisition, with undisclosed terms. With no sourced revenue or later round, the outcome looks like a modest product and team acquisition by a media platform that wanted video capabilities.
notes: Funding unverified: Seedtable and Village.ai list a seed of about 120 thousand USD in 2017-08 from YC and the Tezos Foundation (Tezos is doubtful), PitchBook lists Facebook Marketing API Accelerator and Plug and Play; only aggregators, so no round recorded. PitchBook says founded 2013 while Indivio joined YC in 2017; founded_year left null. Acquisition announcement dated 2022-01 (PitchBook 2022-01-10, CMSWire article 2022-01-20); price not disclosed. No competitor coverage dated near 2017 found (Idomoo and Vidyard appear in undated vendor comparisons only). Dealroom and similar pages were not opened.
